hook.line: The man from Altamira walks into the café and sizes everyone up. Spanish has a vivid way to say that someone treats you as beneath them.
hook.es: El señor de Altamira miró a Tomás por encima del hombro.
hook.en: The man from Altamira looked down on Tomás.

examples.es: El señor de Altamira miró a Tomás por encima del hombro.
examples.en: The man from Altamira looked down on Tomás.

examples.es: Le molesta que la miren por encima del hombro.
examples.en: It bothers her when people look down on her.

examples.es: Hernando nunca mira a nadie por encima del hombro.
examples.en: Hernando never looks down on anyone.

examples.es: Me miró de arriba abajo y no dijo nada.
examples.en: He looked me up and down and said nothing.

examples.es: ¿Por qué me miras por encima del hombro?
examples.en: Why are you looking down on me? (to a friend)

examples.es: Los vecinos nos miran por encima del hombro.
examples.en: The neighbours look down on us.

rule:
*Mirar por encima del hombro* is "to look over the shoulder" at someone, as if they were beneath you: to look down on them. English looks *down*; Spanish looks *over the shoulder*.
The person looked down on comes before the verb as a small word (*me miró*, *la miran*, *nos miran*) or after *a* (*miró a Tomás*).
*Mirar de arriba abajo* is to look someone up and down, sizing them up, often with judgement.
With nobody on the receiving end, it is just a glance behind you: *Miré por encima del hombro.*
smallPrint: Teachers call this an idiom: the words together mean something other than their parts.

readAndPick.es: Me miró por encima del hombro cuando le pregunté el precio.
options: I looked down on him when I asked him the price.
He looked down on me when I asked him the price.

readAndPick.es: Le molesta que la miren por encima del hombro.
options: It bothers her when she looks down on people.
It bothers her when people look down on her.

readAndPick.es: Nos miraron por encima del hombro en el restaurante.
options: They looked down on us at the restaurant.
We looked down on them at the restaurant.

readAndPick.es: Me miró de arriba abajo y no dijo nada.
options: He looked at me and said nothing.
He looked me up and down and said nothing.

readAndPick.es: Hernando nunca mira a nadie por encima del hombro.
options: Hernando always looks down on everyone.
Hernando never looks down on anyone.

readAndPick.es: ¿Por qué me miras por encima del hombro?
options: Why do I look down on you?
Why do you look down on me? (to a friend)

readAndPick.es: Los vecinos nos miran por encima del hombro.
options: We look down on the neighbours.
The neighbours look down on us.

readAndPick.es: Miré por encima del hombro y no había nadie.
options: I looked down on everyone and there was nobody there.
I glanced over my shoulder and there was nobody there.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *me* or *lo*, then type the whole sentence: ___ miró por encima del hombro. (He looked down on me.)
yourTurn.answer: Me miró por encima del hombro.
accept: Él me miró por encima del hombro.
yourTurn.why: The person looked down on is *me*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *la* or *le*, then type the whole sentence: Le molesta que ___ miren por encima del hombro. (It bothers her when people look down on her.)
yourTurn.answer: Le molesta que la miren por encima del hombro.
yourTurn.why: She is the one being looked at, so the small word is *la*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: Hernando never looks down on anyone.
yourTurn.answer: Hernando nunca mira a nadie por encima del hombro.
accept: Hernando no mira a nadie por encima del hombro.
yourTurn.why: *A nadie* names the person looked at, so it needs *a*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: The neighbours look down on us.
yourTurn.answer: Los vecinos nos miran por encima del hombro.
accept: Nos miran por encima del hombro los vecinos.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: She looked me up and down. (a woman did it)
accept: Ella me miró de arriba abajo.
yourTurn.why: *De arriba abajo* is the up and down look.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it a question to a friend: *Me miras por encima del hombro.* becomes: Why are you looking down on me? (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: ¿Por qué me miras por encima del hombro?
yourTurn.why: *Por qué* opens the question and the rest stays the same.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about her: *Me miran por encima del hombro.* becomes: They look down on her.
yourTurn.answer: La miran por encima del hombro.
accept: Ellos la miran por encima del hombro.
A ella la miran por encima del hombro.
yourTurn.why: Swap *me* for *la* to move the look onto her.

pitfalls.wrong: Miró a mí por encima del hombro.
pitfalls.right: Me miró por encima del hombro.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The person looked down on is a small word before the verb: *me*, *la*, *nos*.
Almost. The look goes both ways: *de arriba abajo*.

pitfalls.right: Me miró por encima del hombro.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The fixed phrase is *por encima del hombro*, with no swaps.

personal: Tell me about a place where people look down on others, or a time it happened to you. Use *me miró…* or *nos miran…*.
